messages:
tess: hi! first-day setup question — my Mac enrolled but the app store and internal sites are failing with certificate errors after MDM applied. says 'This connection is not private' and shows our corporate CA as untrusted. any ideas?

it-bot: Device registered: tess-device-1778004321. MDM profile applied. Certificate profile push: completed.

itops: hey tess, welcome! looks like the root CA profile probably pushed but didn't mark as trusted for system level because enrollment was user-approved. did you enroll at OOBE or post-setup?

tess: enrolled after finishing setup (I followed the link from the onboarding email).

sam: that explains it — user-approved MDM installs certs for the user keychain but not the system trust store. we need it supervised to push a system-trusted root. short-term fix: import the company root cert into System Keychain and set to Always Trust (requires admin). julia can grant you temporary admin to do that.

julia: granted temporary admin for 4 hours and sent you a DM with next steps. quick safe command (use only after confirming cert file): sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain /path/to/redwood-root.cer

tess: got the admin and cert file, running the command now. after restarting Safari internal sites load fine, thanks! App Store still shows an error on updates though.

itops: App Store sometimes caches trust until a full reboot or until the system service reloads certs. try rebooting and running softwareupdate --background-critical or open App Store > Updates.

tess: rebooted, App Store updates working. one last Q: should we change anything so future new-hires don't hit this?

sam: we'll update onboarding docs to remind new-hires to wait for the supervised enrollment during OOBE. devex will add a troubleshooting snippet for the certificate trust steps and a note about requesting temporary admin in case a device is user-enrolled.

julia: revoking your admin in ~3.5h. welcome to Redwood :tada:
